data.cultural_impact: * In Islamic culture, the lunar calendar is used to determine the beginning and end of months and the dates of Islamic holidays. Thilaal refers to the third night of the Islamic month of Sha'ban, which is considered an auspicious night. It is believed that making du'a (supplications) and performing good deeds on this night can bring blessings throughout the year. (Source: IslamicFinder.org)
data.spiritual_significance: * The spiritual significance of the name Thilaal is deeply rooted in the Islamic belief in the cycles of nature and the importance of staying connected to God. The number three is believed to be a sacred number in Islamic tradition, as it represents the three main stages of human life: childhood, adulthood, and old age. Thilaal is a reminder that we are continually moving through these stages of life and that we should strive to remain devoted to God at all times.

historical_references.context: During the period when Caliph Omar Ibn Al-Khattab ruled over the Islamic State, there was a significant military campaign in Egypt. One of the commanders, named Thilaal, led the Egyptian troops in several battles against the Byzantines. Thilaal was well-known for his bravery and leadership skills, which played a crucial role in the expansion of the Islamic State in Egypt.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam's Futuh Misr: The Conquest of Egypt, Section 9 - The Battle of Heliopolis and the Death of Amr ibn al-As
historical_references.context: In the year 21 AH (640 AD), Amr ibn al-As led the Islamic army in the Battle of Heliopolis against the Byzantines. During this battle, Thilaal, the commander of the left flank of the Islamic army, was killed. Thilaal's death was a significant loss for the Islamic forces as he was a brave and capable leader. Despite his death, the Islamic army was able to secure a victory in the battle, leading to the eventual conquest of Egypt.
